what: Every plant label in the gatefly lane, extracted statically from source so a lane in another repository can resolve a citation by name and notice when it is reworded or removed.
repository: github.com/rj45Thompson/anchor-demo (separate repo, primary checkout, NOT a linked worktree)
caveat: Presence of a label, not evidence that the plant is reached, can fail, or asserts anything true. A vacuously passing plant is listed here too.
why_this_count_is_lower_than_a_runtime_c: These are CALL SITES. A _plant() inside a loop runs several times and a selftest reports each execution, so a runtime sweep counts more. Measured 2026-11-18: 277 static against 286 runtime over the same 22 modules, and the whole +9 is the three loop sites listed under loops_by_module (ladder_probe +4, uml_kaos +4, reevaluate +1). Every other module agrees exactly. Neither number is wrong; they count different things.
why_a_source_grep_is_not_enough: 84 of 444 labels (18.9%) CANNOT be found by grepping a single line of their own source module, because a long label is written as implicitly concatenated string literals and no one line holds it. This is the failure that produced the snipershot lane's BROKEN LINK on the R7 row: it cited the full sentence, the label was plainly in the file, and a line-by-line grep could not see it. In this file every label is stored joined on one line, so a grep of THIS file finds all 444. That is what makes the manifest load-bearing rather than a convenience.
